Preserve password/code/link authentication, CAPTCHA gating and failed-code budgets, SSO-only no-fallback behavior, mixed-case email binding and other-account code rejection, inactive users, provisional/terms completion, generic credential errors and lockout/unlock, cookie configuration writes, return destinations, session/push cleanup and server challenge/proof revocation. Combined the two identical138-candidate source universes with all original controller and real-CSRF integration cases retained; Session/proof declarations introduce no extra method candidates. Strengthened independent bounce-only and complaint-only resets, logout secret rotation/response/idempotence, invalid pending-link cleanup and blank-password failure-budget preservation, and added consumed-link staging/stale-initial-lookup recheck cases. The current full matrix catches123/138 versus107/138 in the earlier controller profile, with no uncovered/error/timeout rows. Remaining telemetry calls/reason tags and logout flash are unasserted. For normal nonnegative mail counters, >=0/forced-reset variants add an otherwise unnecessary zero-value write; its cost is not measured. Missing code/email presence guards can add unmatched lookups under normal valid-account/token contracts; do not generalize to unsupported legacy records. Removal of the dummy BCrypt operation is an explicit unverified timing-defense gap: equal response messages do not establish equal authentication timing. No tests or defense layers were deleted.

controllers/admin/users_controller.decision: Read the endpoint methods, Admin::BaseController and the paired scenarios. Retain signed-out/non-admin refusal, one-time sign-in link creation and POST-only routing, secret-free account display, permitted/invalid profile updates, exact background-operation actors and targets, bulk selection/action failures and identity deletion restricted to the selected owner. Instance administration is separate from ordinary group coordination and is now measured through the inherited guard source as its own27-candidate context. The endpoint74-candidate profile has no uncovered rows; its remaining survivors expose unasserted redirect responses after several queued operations/identity deletion and absent coordinator/verification/deactivation/locale/date filter combinations. Forcing empty search still matches ordinary rows and changes query work; malformed bulk-ID exception behavior is not pinned here. Keep operation and actor distinctions even when worker setup produces shared kills. No endpoint or scenario was removed.

permissions/instance_administration.decision: Reviewed the shared browser operator guard and pagination against both real admin controller suites. Signed-out and ordinary-user reads are denied, permitted operator reads and protected jobs still work; remove/force-admin authorization mutations are killed. Two surviving removal/true mutations skip authenticate_user! but current_user still resolves through the shared helper and the subsequent is_admin? check still denies ordinary and signed-out users; this does not prove authentication-side-effect equivalence. Pagination survivors show missing multi-page, negative/oversized page and grouped-count response assertions. Changing > to >= assigns the identical boundary page. Preserve browser operators separately from group coordinators, B3 keys and explicit-recipient export jobs; this27-candidate matrix certifies none of those other boundaries.

controllers/api/v1/profile_controller.decision: Retain distinct current-user profile, legal completion, local-login-disabled password handling, other-session/subscription/token cleanup, provider avatar, notification preference, contactability and unsubscribe-token denial cases. The before_action already rejects visitors before me, and resource falls back to current_user, explaining why the action-local checks survive without implying these shared guards may be removed. Remaining gaps include merge-mail rate-limit denial, successful save_experience versus only missing/unauthorized requests, successful email-key read/reset/deactivation/reminder/avatar-upload, invitation index and timezone lists, multiple provider identities/non-OAuth labels and response payloads for mutation actions. The invalid-experience mutation can always reject because there is no positive control for that workflow. Keep private serializers and credential disclosure boundaries explicit; success status or token-scope denial alone does not establish every successful response field.

serializers/poll_serializer.decision: Reviewed source and direct serializer cases with the expanded real anonymous, poll API and vote-reply callers. Current39/80 retains shared omission versus personal voter state, cached membership presence/absence, revoked/rejoined voter access and identified/anonymous hidden-result defenses. Remaining survivors include positive closed/identified participation counters, STV results/type inclusion, anonymous submitted=true, direct-author voting access, legacy reason counts, cached outcome and poll-option names, Markdown mentions and identified my_stance. Several nil mutations suppress fields rather than disclose them; do not classify every survivor as a privacy leak or equivalent. The earlier group_id method is shadowed by the later definition; removed_poll_option_ids has no selected execution and no serialization declaration. Preserve raw four uncovered rows and all named role/cross-channel cases; this one source matrix cannot establish anonymous export/search/realtime safety.

Current71/363 is a narrow cross-output integration profile: BLT, meeting and STV rendering and many generic chart/title/body/rule sections are outside these five examples. Each/map side-effect or wrapper-removal survivors do not authorize removing either a view or its tests. Anonymous identities/results hiding require their own retained storage/export/API cases; weighted examples cannot establish those boundaries. Exact metadata/column placement, nonzero fractions, avatars/chart costs and full publication payloads remain gaps.

Keep PostgreSQL-confirmed blocking rather than sleeps, bounded lock timeout, topic-before-poll lock order, move-owner retry, discard/close permission rechecks before writes or hidden reason publication, query-cache invalidation, destruction without per-item lock queries, recount/increment serialization and reply-tree/count preservation. Existing scenarios protect different interleavings and output invariants despite common setup kills. The broad Comment/Poll/Topic source union includes result calculation, notifications, invitations, ordinary update/read preferences and many unrelated lifecycle methods; their survivors/uncovered entries are explicit gaps of this concurrency selection and have separate canonical profiles. Complete mutation rows do not establish exhaustive schedules or absence of deadlocks. ApplicationRecord named_id remains uncovered. Preserve all concurrency cases; no source or test removal, and no claim that setup-induced common kills make race assertions redundant.

services/mobile/authentication_service.decision: Reviewed the complete 128-candidate profile with 113 killed, 15 survived and no uncovered/error/timeout/no-verdict rows against the authentication service and service/token/web-session/device callers. Retain usable persisted access-token/scopes/TTL controls, PKCE with correctly matching challenges for malformed verifier format tests, public-client and callback refusal before code consumption, expired/used/unknown code and refresh denial, refresh rotation/reuse family revocation, inactive-device rejection, one-use web-session ticket and credential purpose separation. Surviving stored client/callback comparison can be masked by fixed public-client constants and upstream validation, but is retained as a separate binding defense. Prefix checks can be masked by purpose-HMAC lookup and later usable checks; no broad token equivalence. Remaining last-seen/telemetry, replacement-ticket consumption, response refresh-expiry near absolute deadline and long device-name truncation are gaps. Code input validation and persisted authorization binding are different contracts; no token, replay, session or permission tests removed.

Keep revoked guest cleanup on joining/revocation, guest access granted after departure as a separate later state, accepted/pending/inactive invitation boundaries, organization-wide redemption without duplication, cast-vote preservation/restoration only in active polls, transaction rollback of access/votes/counts/notifications, quiet-channel preferences and cross-group/invalid weight denial. Shared allowed-actor examples do not discriminate every service authorization removal. Remaining invitation-already-used and actor-resolution alternatives, realtime access payload/after-commit timing, cached title/delegate updates, empty/missing weight sets and helper returns are gaps; ordinary preference, administrator, delegate removal and experience paths are uncovered here but retain distinct canonical API cases. each/map and nil-return mutations can preserve side effects with ignored returns; no general equivalence or test-deletion claim. All original role/lifecycle cases retained.

Preserve depth/ancestry repair and rollback, discarded/orphan recovery, direct/public/private moves with participant-only retention and anonymous-conversion denial, scheduled-poll guest invitations, plus ordinary allowed/denied pin/tags/read/seen/volume/dismiss/recall behavior. Pre/post-lock authorization layers can mask individual removals; retain both. Attachment group transfer, actual access/reindex/job/realtime payloads, invitation announcement variants and some direct-reader flags remain gaps. Generic update, digest windows, legacy resequencing, preview extraction and missing-root repair branch are unverified by this selection. Integrity tests deliberately corrupt child counts but do not independently distinguish every sequence/position/depth/parent diagnostic; do not treat their surviving checks as equivalent. SQL tree operations are outside much of this fault model. No isolated group invitation fixture substitutes for topic access, and no tests removed.

services/poll_markdown_results_service.decision: Reviewed expanded complete 170-candidate matrix with 106 killed, 57 survived and seven uncovered against canonical renderer examples and real ThreadMarkdownService callers. Retain named submitted/undecided voter output, anonymous omission, until-vote/until-close handling, canonical simple result columns, Markdown escaping and standalone meeting/STV table smoke cases. The thread caller broadens real identity/privacy coverage but does not itself test meeting or STV variants. Existing one-round STV and voter-free meeting structs cannot distinguish many elected/tied/surplus/first-versus-final round and availability-cell changes; those raw survivors remain explicit numeric/format gaps. Missing STV results fallback, multi-round status transitions, none-of-the-above, variable-score voter labels and nil/fraction number formatting are not all established. The anonymous label helper can be bypassed by the earlier anonymous-voter early return, so its survivor does not justify identity exposure or removing anonymity checks. No format or privacy cases removed.
